USMLE-style practice · Pathology

Compensatory growth after resection

Choose the single best answer, then reveal the explanation.

A healthy adult donates part of the liver. During recovery, growth signals drive surviving hepatocytes into the cell cycle, helping restore functional tissue mass. Which adaptive process is most directly demonstrated by this increase in hepatocyte number?

  1. Compensatory hyperplasia
  2. Squamous metaplasia
  3. Coagulative necrosis
  4. Disuse atrophy
  5. Dystrophic calcification
Reveal answer and explanation
Correct answer

Compensatory hyperplasia

Division of surviving hepatocytes increases their number after tissue loss.

Understanding the options

Compensatory hyperplasia
Division of surviving hepatocytes increases their number after tissue loss.
Squamous metaplasia
No replacement by squamous cells is described.
Coagulative necrosis
Necrosis is cell death, not regenerative proliferation.
Disuse atrophy
Atrophy would reduce rather than restore tissue mass.
Dystrophic calcification
Calcium deposition does not restore hepatocyte numbers.
